# Cloud Sync Rules - Default Configuration
#
# These rules determine which files are included/excluded during cloud sync operations.
# The syntax follows the same pattern as .gitignore, where:
#   + pattern = explicitly include matching files/directories
#   - pattern = explicitly exclude matching files/directories
#
# Rules are processed in order and THE FIRST MATCH WINS - a later rule cannot
# override an earlier one. This is why the catch-all "- /**" sits at the very
# bottom, and why an exclusion must appear ABOVE any include that would
# otherwise match the same file.
# Using /** matches files recursively through all subdirectories.

# Databases and their sidecars, before anything else can include them.
# A database is the one file a player cannot resolve by hand if two devices
# both write it, and rclone replaces files wholesale rather than merging, so a
# synced database loses one side's history outright. Copying one mid-write also
# yields a torn file, and a .db separated from its -wal can lose recent writes
# or refuse to open. Ours lives in /storage/.cache and is never synced; this
# guards against one an emulator drops into a save directory.
- /**/*.db
- /**/*.db-wal
- /**/*.db-shm
- /**/*.db-journal
- /**/*.sqlite
- /**/*.sqlite3

# Start by explicitly including directories we want to fully backup
+ /savefiles/**
+ /savestates/**
+ /screenshots/**

# Include specific save file types across all directories
+ /**/*.srm
+ /**/*.sav
+ /**/*.fs
+ /**/*.state*
+ /**/*.auto
+ /**/*.dsv*

# Standalone N64 saves sit BESIDE THE ROM, not in a save directory: every
# shipped mupen64plus.cfg sets SaveSRAMPath = "/storage/roms/n64", so the
# emulator writes n64/<Game>.eep, .mpk, .sra and .fla there. The
# /n64/save/*.eep lines below match the libretro layout and have never
# matched these, so a standalone N64 player's saves have never been backed
# up on any device (#89, D-CLOUD-086). Widened here rather than in the
# per-system block because the four extensions belong to no other system
# and the same file can appear at either depth.
+ /**/*.eep
+ /**/*.mpk
+ /**/*.sra
+ /**/*.fla

# Include system-specific save directories
+ /n64/save/*.eep
+ /n64/save/*.mpk
+ /n64/save/*.sra
+ /n64/save/*.srm
+ /psx/memcards/*.mcd
+ /psx/memcards/*.mcr
+ /dc/shared/savefiles/**
+ /psp/PPSSPP/**

# Backup files
+ /backup/*.zip
+ /backup/*.tar.gz

# Specifically exclude directories that should never be backed up
- /roms/**
- /bios/**
- /downloads/**
- /.cache/**
- /images/**
- /manuals/**
- /videos/**
- /themes/**
- /**/*.bin
- /**/*.iso
- /**/*.img
- /**/*.rom
- /**/*.zip
- /**/*.7z
- /**/*.chd
- /**/*.dol
- /**/*.elf

# Exclude XML files (like gamelist.xml) by default
- /**/*.xml

# Exclude everything else not explicitly included above
- /**

sa/f-pl020h/usrconfig/cloud_sync.conf.de.text:
# Cloud Sync Default Configuration
# This file defines the default values used when creating a new configuration

# Where things live
# ----------------
# Three kinds of thing move through cloud sync, and each key below says which:
#
#   settings  the configuration archive `backuptool` writes: emulator and
#             interface settings, input mapping, themes, collections, bezels.
#             No saves, no ROMs, no operating system.
#   saves     game saves, save states, and screenshots -- files copied in
#             place, matched by cloud_sync-rules.txt
#   content   ROMs and BIOS files
#
# Keys ending in _REMOTE are folders on the cloud remote; the others are on
# this device. Older configs used BACKUPPATH, RESTOREPATH, BACKUPFOLDER,
# SYNCPATH, SYNCPATH_BACKUP and CONTENTPATH; cloud_sync_helper carries a
# customised value across to the new name once, and the old keys are then
# ignored. RESTOREPATH is gone: saves have one local folder, and a config
# that still points it somewhere else makes every saves transfer refuse.

# Saves on this device. Game saves, save states, and screenshots are found
# under here by the rules file.
DEFAULT_SAVESPATH="/storage/roms"

# Settings backups on this device (written by backuptool)
DEFAULT_SETTINGS_BACKUPS="/storage/roms/backup"

# Saves on the cloud remote
DEFAULT_SAVES_REMOTE="/pixelelated/Saves"

# Settings backups on the cloud remote. Must be a sibling of SAVES_REMOTE,
# never inside it -- a mirror of the saves folder would delete the archives.
DEFAULT_SETTINGS_REMOTE="/pixelelated/Backups"

# ROMs and BIOS files on the cloud remote, one folder per system plus "bios".
# Previously unset, which put them at the remote root and scattered system
# folders among whatever else lived there.
#
# Unlike the saves folder this key is derived for an upgrading config rather
# than defaulted, so a device set up under an older layout keeps its ROMs
# beside its saves -- except a saves folder at the top level (/GAMES), which
# has no parent to put them beside: that config gets "" (the remote root,
# where its ROMs already were) for its owner to set. Clear it back to "" to
# use the remote root.
DEFAULT_CONTENT_REMOTE="/pixelelated/Content"

# Logging Options
# --------------
# Set the minimum level of messages to log (INFO, WARN, ERROR)
DEFAULT_LOG_LEVEL="INFO"

# Transfer Settings
# ---------------
# rclone sync rules - modify these options to change transfer behavior
# IMPORTANT: Each option must be preceded by a backslash (\) except the first one
# The saves allowlist (--filter-from /storage/.config/cloud_sync-rules.txt) is
# applied whether or not it appears here: dropping it from this line does not
# drop it from the transfer (#71). To change what syncs, edit the rules file.
DEFAULT_RCLONEOPTS="--progress \
--log-file /var/log/cloud_sync.log \
--filter-from /storage/.config/cloud_sync-rules.txt"

# Network bounds
# --------------
# Timeouts and retry limits for every rclone command the cloud scripts run
# against the cloud -- transfers, listings, probes, the settings archive's
# upload and its size check. Without them rclone's own defaults apply: a
# 60 s connect timeout, a 5 minute idle timeout, 10 low-level retries and
# 3 whole-run retries, so a Wi-Fi link that drops in the middle of a run
# holds the process for well over ten minutes. On the RG SP that left the
# startup sync's card frozen at 113/113 with the launch gate held (#101,
# #102).
#
# --timeout is rclone's IDLE timeout: it fires when no byte has moved for
# that long, so a large transfer that is making progress is unaffected.
# Size it for a stalled link, not a slow one. That is what bounds a dead
# link, and it is the part that matters for #101/#102.
#
# The two retry counts are different things and only one of them may be cut.
# --retries is whole-run: a failed run is repeated by the exit sync, the next
# boot, or the player, so one attempt is right and the run is not repeated
# here. --low-level-retries is per HTTP operation, and it is what every
# rclone user relies on to ride out a provider's transient errors. Cutting it
# to 2 broke Dropbox outright: Dropbox serialises writes per folder and
# answers concurrent ones with a lock error, so a saves backup that replaced
# more than one file failed every time -- the exit sync after a game, for a
# save already in the cloud, which is the ordinary case. Measured on the
# maintainer's RG SP (2026-09-10): replacing 12 files, 6 moves failed at 2
# low-level retries and 0 failed at 10. It is back at rclone's default.
#
# One line, split on spaces by the scripts. An empty value gives these same
# numbers, never rclone's defaults: the scripts fall back to them.
DEFAULT_RCLONE_NET_OPTS="--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 10 --retries 1"
DEFAULT_RCLONE_SYNC_NET_OPTS="--contimeout 5s --timeout 5s --retries 1 --max-duration 90s --low-level-retries 5 --transfers 1"
DEFAULT_SYNC_CEILING_SECONDS=90

# Backup Options
# -------------
## Backup method
### The default is "copy", which sends each save that differs and never deletes
### anything in the cloud; whatever it replaces is kept for one cycle in the
### folder beside the saves folder named <saves folder>-replaced.
### "sync" also deletes from the cloud whatever this device does not have --
### every other device's saves, in a folder they share. It is honoured if set
### here; no menu offers it.
### --delete-excluded is removed from RCLONEOPTS before every run, whatever
### this file says, so a mirror never reaches past the rules file.
DEFAULT_BACKUPMETHOD="copy"

## How many dated settings backups to keep in the cloud, per device
### Each is a full archive (~17MB). Older ones beyond this are removed
### after a successful upload. Set to a larger number to keep more
### history, at the cost of cloud storage.
### Only archives carrying this device's name, between the date and
### ROCKNIX (<date>-<device>-ROCKNIX_SETTINGS.tar.gz), are counted and
### removed; one carrying another device's name, or none, is left alone.
DEFAULT_CLOUD_BACKUP_KEEP="3"

## Enable backing-up the settings backup file
### The default is "yes", which will include the settings backup file in the backup
### Switching to "no" will exclude the settings backup file from the backup
DEFAULT_BACKUPFILE_BACKUP_OPTION="yes"

# Restore Options
# --------------
## Restore method
### The default is "copy", which will preserve any existing files and folders
### Switching to "sync" will replace all local files in the restore path with what is on the remote
DEFAULT_RESTOREMETHOD="copy"

## Enable restoring the settings backup file
### The default is "no", which will exclude the settings backup file from the restore
### Switching to "yes" will include the settings backup file in the restore
DEFAULT_BACKUPFILE_RESTORE_OPTION="no"

sa/shim/rclone.text:
#!/bin/bash
# The image's rclone, with the calls /ctl/fail names ("<ERE><tab><exit>")
# failed instead; /ctl/kill ("<ERE><tab><n>") kills the caller's whole
# process group at the n-th matching call, before it runs -- a kill, not a
# failure; /ctl/post ("<ERE><tab><command>") runs a command after a
# matching call -- another
# writer landing between two steps; /ctl/nohash makes `backend features`
# describe a remote with no hashes (WebDAV, SFTP, SMB, FTP).
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/argv
# A successful provider-features fixture must contain a valid answer.
if [ "$1" = backend ] && [ "$2" = features ] && [ -s /ctl/provider-features ]; then
    cat /ctl/provider-features; exit 0
fi
if [ -s /ctl/fail ]; then
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r pat code; do
        [ -n "${pat}" ] || continue
        if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -qE -- "${pat}"; then
            printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/fault-fired
            echo "ERROR : injected failure ${code}" >&2
            exit "${code}"
        fi
    done < /ctl/fail
fi
if [ -s /ctl/kill ]; then
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r pat nth; do
        [ -n "${pat}" ] || continue
        printf '%s' "$*" | grep -qE -- "${pat}" || continue
        n=$(( $(cat /ctl/kill.count 2>/dev/null || echo 0) + 1 )); echo "${n}" > /ctl/kill.count
        [ "${n}" -eq "${nth}" ] && kill -9 -- "-$(cut -d' ' -f5 /proc/self/stat)"
    done < /ctl/kill
fi
if [ -s /ctl/hang ]; then
    # /ctl/hang ("<ERE><tab><seconds>"): a call that sits silent, as a cloud
    # that accepts and never answers leaves it -- one process, so whatever
    # bound ends the call ends it.
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r pat secs; do
        [ -n "${pat}" ] || continue
        printf '%s' "$*" | grep -qE -- "${pat}" && exec sleep "${secs}"
    done < /ctl/hang
fi
if [ -e /ctl/nohash ] && [ "$1" = backend ] && [ "$2" = features ]; then
    printf '{\n\t"Name": "qa",\n\t"Hashes": [],\n\t"Features": {\n\t\t"BucketBased": false\n\t}\n}\n'
    exit 0
fi
if [ -s /ctl/post ]; then
    /sa/rclone.real "$@"; rc=$?
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r pat cmd; do
        [ -n "${pat}" ] || continue
        printf '%s' "$*" | grep -qE -- "${pat}" && eval "${cmd}"
    done < /ctl/post
    exit "${rc}"
fi
exec /sa/rclone.real "$@"
